history: Fuzhou was founded in 202 BC; its banyan trees gave it the name 'Banyan City'. The Three Lanes and Seven Alleys, a 'living fossil' of the old ward system, raised modern stars like Lin Zexu, Yan Fu and Lin Juemin. Mawei Shipyard was the cradle of China's modern navy; lacquerware and Shoushan stone carving are the city's treasures.
importance: Capital of Fujian · Banyan City · Gateway of the Maritime Silk Road
foods: King of Fujian cuisine — abalone, sea cucumber and shark fin simmered eight hours.
Yonghe fish balls, thin skin and fragrant filling — the taste of home.
Wrappers beaten from meat; the 'swallow skin' dish opens every banquet.
Pork carved to bloom like a lychee — sweet, sour and springy.
Thin rice sheets scraped at the pot rim, with shrimp-oil flavor.
Peanut soup so soft you need no teeth, served with taro paste.
Steamed taro paste with lard and sugar — king of Fujian desserts.
Fuzhou olives, sweet after the bite — fragrant candied fruit.
scenes: 'Half of modern Chinese history' — Lin Juemin's former home.
Yongquan Temple and cliff carvings; climb for river views.
A 1,700-year-old garden from the Jin dynasty.
Old consulates and western houses — an artsy quarter.
The cradle of China's modern navy.
Old merchant quarter, picture-like at night.
A steel walkway through the forest canopy.
Blue-tears glow and stone-built fishing villages.
